title: Isomorphisms of coherent formal modules are detected on an open cover
statement: Let $X$ be a Noetherian scheme (a locally Noetherian scheme [pqf-def-locnoeth] whose underlying space is quasi-compact), $\mathcal I\subseteq\mathcal O_X$ a quasi-coherent sheaf of ideals, $X=\bigcup_{j\in J}U_j$ an open covering, and $\alpha=(\alpha_n)_{n\ge1}:(\mathcal F_n)\to(\mathcal G_n)$ a morphism in $\mathit{Coh}(X,\mathcal I)$ [def-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-module]. For an $\mathcal O_X$-linear map $\varphi:\mathcal F\to\mathcal G$ of $\mathcal O_X$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] and an open $U\subseteq X$, $\varphi|_U:\mathcal F|_U\to\mathcal G|_U$ denotes the $\mathcal O_X|_U$-linear map with components $(\varphi|_U)_W=\varphi_W$ for the opens $W\subseteq U$. If for every $j\in J$ and every $n\ge1$ the map $\alpha_n|_{U_j}:\mathcal F_n|_{U_j}\to\mathcal G_n|_{U_j}$ is an isomorphism of $\mathcal O_X|_{U_j}$-modules, then $\alpha$ is an isomorphism in $\mathit{Coh}(X,\mathcal I)$: there is a morphism $\beta:(\mathcal G_n)\to(\mathcal F_n)$ of $\mathit{Coh}(X,\mathcal I)$ with $\beta\circ\alpha=\mathrm{id}$ and $\alpha\circ\beta=\mathrm{id}$; moreover each $\alpha_n$ is an isomorphism of $\mathcal O_X$-modules and $\beta_n=\alpha_n^{-1}$.

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma 087X (lemma-inverse-systems-abelian), proof after the affine construction: a morphism whose components are isomorphisms is an isomorphism; exactness is checked on an open covering

proof.text: (Each $\alpha_n$ is an isomorphism of $\mathcal O_X$-modules.) Fix $n$ and write $U_{jk}=U_j\cap U_k$. Restriction is compatible with composition and identities and with iterated restriction: $(\psi\varphi)|_V=\psi|_V\varphi|_V$, $\mathrm{id}|_V=\mathrm{id}$ and $(\varphi|_U)|_V=\varphi|_V$ for opens $V\subseteq U$, since all three hold on each component $W\subseteq V$ by the definition $(\varphi|_V)_W=\varphi_W$ [lem-weil-pbc-glue-sheaves-of-modules, notation of the statement]. For each $j$ let $\beta_j:\mathcal G_n|_{U_j}\to\mathcal F_n|_{U_j}$ be the $\mathcal O_X|_{U_j}$-linear inverse of $\alpha_n|_{U_j}$ (hypothesis). Restricting the identities $\beta_j\,\alpha_n|_{U_j}=\mathrm{id}$, $\alpha_n|_{U_j}\,\beta_j=\mathrm{id}$ to $U_{jk}$ shows that $\beta_j|_{U_{jk}}$ is a two-sided inverse of $\alpha_n|_{U_{jk}}$; so is $\beta_k|_{U_{jk}}$, and a two-sided inverse is unique ($b=b(ab')=(ba)b'=b'$), hence $\beta_j|_{U_{jk}}=\beta_k|_{U_{jk}}$ for all $j,k$. By glueing of morphisms [lem-weil-pbc-glue-sheaves-of-modules, (1)] there is a unique $\mathcal O_X$-linear $\beta_n:\mathcal G_n\to\mathcal F_n$ with $\beta_n|_{U_j}=\beta_j$ for all $j$. Then $(\alpha_n\beta_n)|_{U_j}=\alpha_n|_{U_j}\beta_j=\mathrm{id}=\mathrm{id}|_{U_j}$ and likewise $(\beta_n\alpha_n)|_{U_j}=\mathrm{id}|_{U_j}$ for every $j$, so by the uniqueness clause of [lem-weil-pbc-glue-sheaves-of-modules, (1)] $\alpha_n\beta_n=\mathrm{id}_{\mathcal G_n}$ and $\beta_n\alpha_n=\mathrm{id}_{\mathcal F_n}$: $\alpha_n$ is an isomorphism of $\mathcal O_X$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] with inverse $\beta_n=\alpha_n^{-1}$.

proof.text: (The inverses commute with the transition maps.) Let $t^{\mathcal F}_n:\mathcal F_{n+1}\to\mathcal F_n$ and $t^{\mathcal G}_n:\mathcal G_{n+1}\to\mathcal G_n$ be the transition maps. As $\alpha$ is a morphism of $\mathit{Coh}(X,\mathcal I)$ [def-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-module, (1)], $t^{\mathcal G}_n\alpha_{n+1}=\alpha_nt^{\mathcal F}_n$. Composing with $\beta_n$ on the left and $\beta_{n+1}$ on the right (step 1) gives $\beta_nt^{\mathcal G}_n\alpha_{n+1}\beta_{n+1}=\beta_n\alpha_nt^{\mathcal F}_n\beta_{n+1}$, i.e. $\beta_nt^{\mathcal G}_n=t^{\mathcal F}_n\beta_{n+1}$ for every $n\ge1$.

proof.text: (Conclusion.) By step 2, $\beta=(\beta_n)_{n\ge1}$ is a family of $\mathcal O_X$-linear maps $\mathcal G_n\to\mathcal F_n$ commuting with the transition maps, i.e. a morphism $(\mathcal G_n)\to(\mathcal F_n)$ of $\mathit{Coh}(X,\mathcal I)$ [def-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-module, (1)]. Composition and identities in $\mathit{Coh}(X,\mathcal I)$ are componentwise [def-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-module, proof step 4], so step 1 gives $\beta\circ\alpha=(\beta_n\alpha_n)=\mathrm{id}$ and $\alpha\circ\beta=(\alpha_n\beta_n)=\mathrm{id}$. Hence $\alpha$ is an isomorphism in $\mathit{Coh}(X,\mathcal I)$ with inverse $\beta$.
